title: Console throttle-friendly MVP: trimmed dashboards, sampled tracing, and compact cost breakdown
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: We need a defensible MVP for Console that preserves core developer value (route cost visibility, basic tracing breadcrumbs, and high-level dashboards) while cutting lower-value surface area to meet timelines and cost constraints. Goal: deliver a "throttle-friendly" default configuration that reduces telemetry volume and tokenized cost operations by 60% compared to the initial scope, with clear fallback behavior for higher tiers.
scope_changes: Remove: per-route granular breakdown card (defer to follow-up) — replace with compact top-5 routes summary
Remove: full-span distributed tracing visualization (defer) — replace with sampled trace links + trace-summary table
Reduce: dashboard tiles from 12 -> 6 macro tiles (aggregate some metrics into a single 'performance' tile)
Add: sampling budget control for tracing with safe defaults (0.5% for free tier, 5% for paid)
Add: compact cost breakdown that groups token cost into 3 buckets (model compute, cache savings, infra overhead) instead of per-stage breakdown
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: 6 macro tiles implemented and visible for new orgs; each tile loads within 1s on average for 95th percentile of requests
Tracing: sampled tracing enabled with default sampling rates; sampled trace link opens to trace-summary table showing trace_id, route, latency_ms, and error flag
Cost: compact cost breakdown implemented and matches backend aggregated numbers within 2% for 24h window
Telemetry budget: aggregated telemetry volume reduction >= 50% vs original detailed-scope baseline during 24h synthetic workload
Rollout: feature gated and can be toggled per-org; canary to 5% of orgs and rollbackable within 15 minutes
Design sign-off: PM + Design approve UI and microcopy for compact tiles and sampled tracing flow
Docs: PRD updated and customer-facing FAQ published describing sampling behavior and how to opt into full telemetry
decisions_log: 2026-02-22: Decided to prioritize 'top-5 routes' summary over per-route card to reduce cardinality and cost (PM + Eng).
2026-02-25: Design proposed microtiles pattern; engineering requested single API for aggregated metrics — accepted with minor adjustments.
2026-03-03: Tracing sampling rates set to 0.5% free / 5% paid; can be overridden via org policy (consensus: reduce telemetry but keep observability for incidents).
2026-03-08: Agreed to postpone real-time per-token cost breakdown and deliver 24-hour aggregated buckets in MVP.
2026-03-09: Release gating: must support org-level toggle and rollback path before GA.
tradeoffs: Lower telemetry volume improves cost and scalability but increases time-to-debug for low-frequency regressions.
Aggregated cost buckets reduce user granularity but let us ship simpler UX and cheaper storage retention.
Sampling tracing reduces storage/ingest costs but requires careful sampling configuration to preserve signal for incidents; we'll provide a manual 'diagnostic mode' for short-term ramp-ups.
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting — aligned on 'throttle-friendly' principle and MVP boundaries.
2026-02-28: Backend API for aggregated metrics proto complete; requires UX wiring.
2026-03-04: Frontend microtiles draft reviewed; design requested copy tweaks for sampling explanation.
2026-03-06: Integration test: compact cost breakdown matches nightly aggregate within 1.7% (good).
2026-03-10: Internal review with Eng + Design — minor accessibility fixes and rollout gating added to acceptance.
Next: schedule canary rollout for 5% of orgs on 2026-03-14 pending infra readiness.
follow_up_tasks: PM: Publish customer FAQ and changelog entry explaining sampled tracing and cost buckets
Eng: Add diagnostic mode endpoint to temporarily increase sampling to 20% for specified orgs
SRE: Implement canary rollback playbook and runbook snippets for on-call
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on measurable acceptance criteria and rollback controls. If sampling rates or cost-bucket boundaries change, update PRD and customer messaging before rollout. Consider adding a short explainer in the Console UI about the tradeoff between telemetry volume and cost.
